surface: The grid as one tab stop (tabNavigation: false): Tab leaves the grid from any cell, Shift+Tab returns to the cell it left, and the arrows still move inside.

steps.note: With tabNavigation off, Tab from a cell in the middle of the grid leaves it for the page's next control. NVDA names it. Finding (unconfirmed, likely the setup): VoiceOver says nothing here on both browsers, where it names the same button when Tab leaves the grid from a row's last cell (default-mode). Two things set this step apart from that one: it is the page's first key, which VoiceOver is silent on in some runs, and VoiceOver still interacts with the grid (this scenario starts in it, default-mode on the page). The Shift+Tab out later in this run, after the reader left the grid, is announced. A run with `start: page` tells the two apart before this is reported as the grid's.
Shift+Tab from the page returns into the grid on the cell it left: its value and its column header.
The arrows still move between cells.
Shift+Tab leaves the grid for the page's previous control, whichever cell has the focus.
Tab from the page returns into the grid on the cell it left.
